editorial:
Imagine being a shy twelve-year-old who sees the world through a camera lens. That is exactly how Sam lives his life. He is obsessed with movies and wants to create something special, so he decides to follow a tough girl named Bobby around for an entire day. The vibe is very sweet and awkward, capturing that weird time in middle school where you are trying to figure out who you are. You will feel for Sam as he tries to make his documentary look more exciting than it actually is, while Bobby just wants to be left alone. It is a charming story about friendship and the lengths people go to for their art.

What really makes this work is the acting from the two kids, who feel like real people rather than scripted actors. The pacing is steady, though it stays mostly in a slice-of-life lane. If you like stories about misfits and growing up, you will love this. For the best experience, you should look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see every detail of Sam's filming style. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to catch it for a movie night. It is a light watch that leaves you feeling good.
endingExplained: By the end, Sam and Bobby form a real bond that goes beyond just a film project. Sam realizes that forcing a story is not as important as the actual friendship he made. The movie wraps up with them accepting each other for who they are. There is no huge shock twist, but rather a heartwarming conclusion where Sam finds confidence and Bobby opens up, showing that they both needed a friend like the other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and creative kids.
